method: 30 BASS rows drawn at random (Python random.Random(2026).sample over all 121 rows). The full 'Test Observations' text of each row was read and given a burn / no-burn answer for the row's initial conditions (or none when the notes do not allow one), then compared with the keyword rule. The reading was done by an AI assistant (Claude), the same model family that wrote the rules, not by an independent human annotator.

items.note: dim blue flame sustained until the fan was turned off
items.observations: difficult to ignite,very dim blue, got some soot at 16:33:51 gbx time,   N2 on at 34:18,    soot faded a bit, still have a pimple of soot,  N2 off at 34:48, fan 42:35:04, all blue flame again, like blue crescent moon.  Fan off at 35:30 ish.  Flame extinuishes right away.  Don noted no soot deposition on the sphere.  Just has bubbles.

items.note: igniter broken, no test
items.observations: Igniter seems to have broken prior to ignition.  No, 1 ohm resistance is still there.  Don trying again.  No go. A different igniter works, so igniter is broken.  No useful digital stills.

items.note: igniter broken, no test
items.observations: Igniter is broken!   Igniter inventory done.  2 good ones left.  No images taken

items.note: 'nice burn', flame reached a steady size
items.observations: nice burn, left igniter on a bit long and then on again.     Camera set to GMT, not MSG.  Appeared to reach a ss size ~ 3 cm long.

items.note: 'wake ign' and flow stepped 7.5 -> 2 cm/s imply a sustained flame, but the notes never say so explicitly
items.observations: wake ign,  3/3 initial frames before bracket.   Still camera only took initial and final set of pics, he didn't repress camera at call, he unlocked it 'reset'.  Igniter failed after this test.

items.note: all-blue flame with soot streaks
items.observations: broke igniter.    All blue with intermittent soot balls streaking back.  Might be able to get flow measurements from those.  Lab view zoomed in on flame also.

items.note: burned 2 s, died when the igniter was turned off
items.observations: Ignited and burned for only 2 s.  Died when igniter turned off.  Repeated re-ignition attempts failed.  Don didn't want it to burn since their flight suits are made of this stuff.  He felt like he should have left the igniter on longer.  Fan cal and GN2 cal  at ~16:00

items.note: ignition in 1.5 min, dim flame visible
items.observations: nice over the shoulder view, very hard to see dim flame in expt video.  Ignition in 1.5 min.

items.note: flame for ~3 min at 9 cm/s, out only when flow shut off
items.observations: (Flame from GMT 15:44:30 to 15:47:10) Ignition at 9 cm/s (FAN 60) then set FAN to 42, then slowly to 41.  After several minutes, shut flow off.  Flame became very dim blue before extinguishing.  Don’s observation: “There was a swelling action with the PMMA in which the fuel vapor coming from the sphere makes the flame swell.”

items.note: stable flame, slow downstream spread
items.observations: ignited well and had initial sooty flame wrapped around leading edge of sample.  Reduced flow to 7 cm/s and flame turned all blue -Emmons shape.  Reached a steady size and spread downstream very slowly, all blue flame.  Top stills look like about 1 cm long flame with curved base and slightly curved tail, mostly oval.   All blue with intermittent yellow streaks.   Very stable.  Spread maybe 1 cm?

items.note: went out when the igniter was retracted, twice
items.observations: tried igniting at 6 cm/s.  Flame went out when igniter was retracted, with a puff of smoke.  Tried a 2nd time, same effect.  3rd try igniter  broke/failed.  Sample showed blackened spot around mid-sample in over the shoulder view at 15:15 GMT.  Stowed igniters in bag.  Last run until January when we get new igniters up.

items.note: candle burned ~10 min
items.observations: P mode is auto-everything. Very long burn (~ 10 min), waited at every flow condition,   steady radiometer at 0.32 pot  ~ 2.2 (lowest for flame).  Consistenly goes out at pot 0.31

items.note: bright sooty flame, later blown out with N2
items.observations: ignited at 62, fan up to 87 then 100,   got long sooty tail, comet.   Envelope flame, very bright and sooty,   then fan to 42, blue LE and sooty tail.   Fan 41, slightly dimmer but still sooty tail.   Joe turned pot to 0.32 (read after) to get minimum flame (very dim blue LE only),    GN2 on max did not blow it out right away, but did eventually extinguish it.  LE blew off and ring flame stabilized for a number of s.   Card full on still camera.  Didn't seem to get the GN2 on the digital stills.  Leaving igniter in msg.  Still fuel left.

items.note: repeated ignitions, flame never sustained
items.observations: repeated ignition attempts, no luck keeping the flame sustained.  After igniter retract, the blue flame leading edge shrinks back, the tail shrinks, the flame becomes parallel to the fuel surface, and then winks out.    Apparently not flammable in opposed flow for the same concurrent flow.  Heat losses are different though, due to the metal holder around the back end of sample but not on front edge.

items.note: candle burning, out when flow stepped to 0
items.observations: Last one with over the shoulder view on this session.    Got hot then stepped to 0 flow, went out.

items.note: candle burned out all wax
items.subtypeNote: rule says flame_spread; a candle burning down is 'burned'
items.observations: same candle, 3rd test,  trying for longer time at low flow. Burned out all wax, only 2 brackets.  Flame got smaller quickly flow rates due to lack of wax.

items.note: long candle burn at low flow
items.observations: LONG candle burn at very low flow rates.  Sooty at 2 cm/s and then at 1 cm/s.   All blue at fan41.  Candle  out at flow change.

items.note: lit on 2nd try, spread around the sphere
items.observations: flame lit on 2nd try,  quickly turned sooty, spread around small remaining sphere.  All blue at lower flows, burned out fuel.  Very nice over the shoulder zoomed in view of flame.  Better than expt video!

items.note: blue flame after 3 min of attempts; out only after fan reduced
items.observations: took about 3 min to ignite, repeated attempts.  Got blue flame that was 1/2 way or mor around top.   Turned fan down in increments:12:10:20 0.6 (43); 11:15 0.5 (42); 11:50 0.35 (41) and 12:35 0.32 (41)   flame self-extinguished.

items.note: flame blown out by N2, so it was burning
items.observations: flame did blow out with GN2 at about a pot 6.

items.note: ignited in 1 min, symmetric growth
items.observations: Ign in 1 min.  Symmetric growth.  Gets sooty, even when flow reduced to 41.  Gets all blue at 18:38, out at 18:40 at finite extremely low flow.

items.note: burned on the forward stagnation region, minimal spread
items.subtypeNote: rule says flame_spread; notes say 'minimal spread', 'burned' fits better
items.observations: broke 2 igniters on this trying to get it to ignite. 3rd one was suspect, and didn't work.  2nd vitiation, got it ignited, burned just on forward stagnation region, minimal spread.  Went out at finite flow.  Post burn shape was crater and protrusion on lower half.

items.note: candle ran out of fuel
items.observations: higher flow test, but ran out of fuel too quickly.

items.note: did not ignite, igniter on the whole test
items.observations: leave igniter on entire test to provide additional heat to flame.  Did not ignite.  Not even any smoke.  Flow too high?

items.note: sooty bullet-shaped flame, out when fan off
items.observations: ignited at 10 cm/s, fan to 42,   less vapor jetting noted, bullet shaped flame, sooty.   Fan to 41, similar, slightly smaller flame.    Fan off flame all blue and pulses a few times before extinguished.  Jay saw cloud go by when he turned on fan at GMT 17:12 ish.

items.note: steady spreading
items.observations: Nice symmetric burn, some soot at 10 cm/s,  Steady spreading, flame seems to reach a steady length.  Decreasing flow shrinks flame and changes to mostly blue, but still spreading.  Gets very dim near end of sample as it shrinks and extinguishes at burnout.  Don noted the fiberglass matrix was still intact after the burn.

items.note: ignited nicely, sooty flame
items.observations: first wax slab test.   Ignited nicely.  Very sooty flame wrapped around leading edge.  Turned flow down to 3 cm/s.  Flame sooty for a while, then as it burned out leading edge it got dimmer, shorter and eventully  all blue.  Shrank slowly and extinguished by itself.

items.note: burning laminar, very fast burning rate
items.observations: Burning laminar but sooty at 42, turned down very slowly to 41 and flame started to turn blue and vapor jet.  Turned fan to max, and flame did not blow off stagnation region.  Burning rate incredibly fast.  Turned off flow right when fuel completely ran out.  Don examined igniter and there is one thin spot, so may not last much longer.

items.note: dim blue flame spreading upwind
items.observations: No Don camera.  Wake flame very dim on video, all blue, spread very slowly upwind.  Ignited GBX time 16:14:44,  N2 on at 16:17:18,  did not extinguish, increased to pot 10, at 16:18:37,  N2 off at 16:19:19.  Accidentaly turned fan up briefly instead of N2.  Fan turned to 40 at 16:19:22, flame and flame went out at 16:19:34.  All times GBX.

items.note: flame spread on the top side, out with flow off
items.observations: Ignited and turned flow down, then N2 on while flame was small and blue.    Flame did not go out completely, but only seemed to spread on the top side of the video view.  It wrapped around quite far on top, but not quite to stag. Region.  Turned N2 off and flame grew and got sottier.  Extinguished with flow off at6.75 minutes or so.  Joe asked about why N2 didn't put out flame.
